newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians tortured prisoner to death - official.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians tortured prisoner to death - official.

text.p: Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Meddein said on Monday a Palestinian held by PLO security forces in the West Bank city of Nablus was tortured to death during interrogation.

The prosecutor-general and justice ministry were investigating the death of Yousef Ismail Al-Baba, 32, in the Palestinian-ruled enclave, Abu Meddein said in the first official confirmation of torture.
He called the case "a flagrant violation of the law since Al-Baba was arrested without an order from the police or from the prosecutor-general".
Human rights groups have accused Palestinian security forces of systematically torturing prisoners and accused the Palestinian Authority of not doing enough to halt the abuse.

The Jerusalem-based Palestinian Society for the Protection of Human Rights and Environment said on Saturday that PLO military intelligence arrested Al-Baba on January 3 on suspicion of making an improper property sale.
Abu Meddein told Reuters that as a result of torture, Al-Baba was hospitalised in Nablus on January 24 but returned to jail the next day before finishing treatment.
"As a result of further torture, his health condition worsened and he died," Abu Meddein said.
"During the investigation we discovered that Al-Baba's medical file had disappeared from Nablus hospital, so we arrested some hospital employees for interrogation," he added.
Yousef's brother Omar Al-Baba said: "We will not bury the body before we receive an official report to clarify the reasons for his death. We believe he was tortured to death."

According to the Washington-based Solidarity International for Human Rights group, 12 Palestinians have been tortured to death while under interrogation since the Palestinian Authority began taking control of the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank in 1994 under interim peace deals with Israel.

The Palestinian Authority denies systematic torture but has investigated prisoners' deaths in detention and promised to fight abuses. In August, a Palestinian military court sentenced three Palestinian policemen to long jail terms after finding them guilty of torturing a prisoner to death.
PLO officials said military intelligence was responsible for most of the cases of human rights abuses and torture.
